pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_port/fixtureCorpus.ts:97 This hand-written type assertion narrows a plain string facet to the Attention union. It is sound only because lines 179 and 248 of the same file write the literals "missing" and "unreadable", which match ATTENTION in packages/domain/src/library.ts:38, and neither the cast nor those writes say so, so an edit that adds a third attention value would keep compiling while the row carries a value the type rules out.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_port/fixtureCorpus.ts:97 Three `as` assertions in this file (lines 66, 76 and 97) override what the checker infers. Each depends on a fact stated somewhere else: a non-empty array at lines 66 and 76, and writes that use only ATTENTION literals at line 97. No site names its dependency, and the depended-on sites (lines 179 and 248) have no note saying the cast relies on them.

pairs.registryProposal: In TypeScript the members this subject would count are mostly `as` assertions, non-null `!` and `any` flow. The golden path names `any` through census-counts-unmarked-members, but no technique states the rule for `as` assertions directly. A short note in soundness-argument-names-its-dependencies saying that a TS `as` narrowing of a wider type is a member, and that a type guard is the removal, would make the subject usable on TS trees.
